title: signal
content_html:
signal

Nerve opens with a sound through fog that might be a foghorn or a siren. Before we know what it means, it makes us attend. Together, the opening and particle signals raise a question about what makes a disturbance reach someone as news, warning or invitation. Noise can obscure a signal, supply context or become the thing a different listener came to hear. Who or what decides when a disturbance counts as a message? A partial message may be recognisable through interference. How much needs to survive for it to be heard as a signal? Nerve · Particle signals 1 a

Reading note. Buddhism. The instruction to Bāhiya asks him to attend to what is heard in the hearing itself. In Nerve, what has reached the listener before they call it a foghorn or a siren? What changes once they hear it as a warning or a summons? Bāhiya Sutta, Ud 1.10
